title: The Crane Doesn't Wait
tagline: A concrete pour scheduled down to the hour, a crew of thirty waiting on your call, and a safety concern that just turned up on the third floor.

wake_up.text: Today's the big pour — the third floor slab, scheduled with the concrete supplier down to the hour. Everything downstream depends on this going right.

choices.text: Review the full pour plan one more time before leaving
Trust yesterday's prep and get moving

site_arrival.text: The site is already stirring — crew arriving, equipment being checked, the concrete trucks scheduled for a nine o'clock arrival.

choices.text: Run the morning safety briefing

random_moment.text: The hour before a big pour has its own particular energy on a site — a little different every time.

choices.text: The crew is unusually sharp and ready this morning
The concrete supplier calls with a minor scheduling concern
The weather forecast is exactly right for a pour today

morning_inspection.text: A final walkthrough of the formwork before the trucks arrive — the last chance to catch anything before concrete makes it permanent.

choices.text: Personally inspect every section of formwork
Spot-check the highest-risk sections only

safety_concern.text: A crew member flags a shoring post on the third floor that looks slightly out of plumb — probably fine, but the trucks are forty-five minutes out and re-checking means possibly delaying a pour that's booked down to the hour.

choices.text: Halt everything and have it rechecked properly before the pour
Do a quick visual confirmation yourself and proceed
Get the structural engineer on site before deciding
Proceed as scheduled — it's probably within tolerance

safety_outcome_halt.text: The recheck finds the post genuinely needed adjustment. The pour gets rescheduled for early afternoon, and every person on that floor is safer for the delay — the kind of call that costs money and is still obviously correct.

choices.text: Coordinate the rescheduled pour

safety_outcome_visual.text: Your own read says it's within tolerance, and the pour proceeds on schedule. It holds — this time — but it was a judgment call made faster than the situation maybe deserved.

choices.text: Proceed with the pour

safety_outcome_engineer.text: The engineer's read is fast and definitive: within tolerance, safe to proceed. A short delay, but everyone on the pour crew works with real confidence instead of a shrug.

choices.text: Proceed with the pour

safety_outcome_proceed.text: The pour goes ahead on schedule. It holds, but the shoring concern never actually got resolved — just outrun by the schedule, which is exactly the kind of decision that catches up with a site eventually.

choices.text: Proceed with the pour

afternoon_pour.text: The pour itself goes smoothly, thirty people moving in careful coordination, concrete filling the forms exactly as planned.

choices.text: Oversee the pour to completion

afternoon_inspection.text: A city inspector arrives for a scheduled check on an unrelated part of the site — electrical rough-in on the second floor.

choices.text: Walk the inspector through personally
Let the lead electrician handle the walkthrough

evening_schedule.text: Tomorrow's schedule needs finalizing — crew assignments, material deliveries, the next phase of work now that today's pour is behind you.

choices.text: Take the time to plan tomorrow in real detail
Rough out tomorrow's plan and refine it in the morning

end_shift.text: The site empties out for the night, thirty people going home safe, and a floor slab curing in the dark that wasn't there this morning.

choices.text: Head home

triumphant.title: Ahead of Schedule, Zero Incidents
triumphant.blurb: Every call today was the right one, including the hard one. This is the day the whole crew will point to.

steady_hand.title: Solid Day on Site
steady_hand.blurb: No incidents, no shortcuts — just careful, competent site management, decision after decision.

ordinary_day.title: Another Milestone Hit
ordinary_day.blurb: A full day of work, a major pour completed. Tomorrow's schedule is already set.

burned_out.title: Running on Empty
burned_out.blurb: You made it through the day, but you're not sure how. This pace, decision after decision, has a real cost.

written_up.title: Safety Review Called
written_up.blurb: Something about today's shoring call is heading into a formal safety review. Everyone's safe. The process still needs a look.
